Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Thanks for the draft order form. Two items popped up in our internal review that we need to flag before legal can sign:

1) Rolling deploy maintenance windows: our infra team cannot accept rolling deploys that impact >10% of capacity during business hours. Can Redwood confirm a carveout or an explicit exclusion for rolling deploys that exceed this threshold?

2) Escalation path: during a rolling deploy incident our oncall needs a direct escalation path to a named Redwood oncall (or secondary) with a 30-minute ack SLA. The current order form references a generic support ladder — we need a more prescriptive clause.

We attached a sample matrix (maintenance_downtime_matrix.xlsx) showing our preferred blackout hours. Priya (cc) is on procurement and will own contract pickup.

Appreciate quick turnaround — legal is on a compressed timeline.

Aditya / Stephanie — sketching a proposal below before I send to Acme. Notes and open questions included.

Proposal (order-form language snippets):
- Maintenance carveout: "Rolling deploys or platform upgrades that temporarily shift up to 15% of serving capacity may be scheduled outside customer-defined blackout hours; Redwood will provide at least 72 hours notice for rolling deploys that affect >10% of capacity and will minimize disruption within agreed maintenance windows."
- Escalation appendix: "For incidents occurring during a scheduled rolling deploy, Redwood will provide a named escalation contact (Oncall Team Lead) and will acknowledge pager notifications within thirty (30) minutes. Further remediation SLAs remain as defined in the MSA."

Open questions:
- Can we push the 15% ceiling as a maximum buffer? (product says yes in most clusters but depends on Dedicated sizing)
- Do we commit to 72 hours notice or 48? 72 is safer for scheduling.

Attachments I plan to send: redlines_orderform_v3.pdf (with inline comments).

If you both sign off I will send to Miguel and cc their legal.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Mar 2029 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form SLA redlines — suggested legal text

Marissa / Stephanie — see legal suggestions below. I kept language narrow to avoid opening wider SLA obligations.

Legal suggestions (Order Form / MSA amendment):
- Maintenance exceptions: "Customer acknowledges that scheduled platform maintenance, including rolling deploys and version upgrades, may temporarily reduce available capacity. Redwood will not be liable for service credits resulting from scheduled maintenance provided Redwood: (i) provides Customer at least seventy-two (72) hours prior notice for rolling deploys expected to impact greater than ten percent (10%) of Customer's allocated capacity; and (ii) schedules such activity, to the extent practicable, outside the Customer's designated blackout hours as set forth in Schedule A."

- Escalation and acknowledgement: "During an incident arising in conjunction with scheduled rolling deploy activities, Redwood will provide a named on-call escalation contact and will use commercially reasonable efforts to acknowledge escalation pages within thirty (30) minutes. Acknowledgement under this Section is not a guarantee of resolution within a specific timeframe and does not modify other SLA remedy provisions, including service credit eligibility."

Notes: 1) We avoid promising remediation times tied to the 30m ack — that remains an operational pledge, not a credit-triggering SLA. 2) The 72-hour notice clause narrows customer expectations; if product presses for 48h we can consider, but legal prefers 72h.

If you want, I can insert these snippets as tracked changes into redlines_orderform_v3.pdf and return for final review.

— Aditya
Counsel, Contracts & Security, Redwood Inference

Miguel — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (AE) and Aditya (legal).

Short summary of our position:
- Rolling deploys: Redwood can accept a carveout that requires 72 hours advance notice for rolling deploys expected to affect >10% of a customer's allocated capacity and will use commercially reasonable efforts to avoid scheduled work during your blackout hours. We set the upper planning buffer at 15% to preserve operational flexibility for Dedicated clusters; that is captured in the attached redline.
- Escalation: Redwood will provide a named oncall escalation contact and will acknowledge pages within 30 minutes. We are not committing remediation times as part of the 30-minute ack — remediation SLAs remain under the existing MSA service credit framework.
